From 915048e6aed264dd7bf68e29ba485ade4c44f845 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Greg Hurrell <greg@hurrell.net>
Date: Fri, 21 Apr 2017 16:29:55 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] Fix edge case regression when searching for dotfiles

Fixes problem introduced in ee9732511.

Given an initial empty search string we were setting dotfiles to have a
score of 0.0 in order to hide them from the search listing, which was
causing them to be skipped in subsequent searches, even if the user
types ".foo". Notably, on pressing backspace, our shortcircuiting would
be deactivated and we would show the results.

The (regrettably subtle) fix here is to hide the files in the initial
search by returning a *negative* score.

When the user then types a period ("."), we will go ahead an calculate
the score, at which point the -1.0 will be replaced with some positive
score (because we can't fail to match in this case, the dot matches the
dotfile by definition). If the *next* letter (or any other letter typed
later on) causes a failure to match, we'll set the score to 0.0, causing
it to be suppressed (until backspace is pressed).

On the other hand, if instead of typing a period the user types a
letter, these files will continue to be skipped (and their score set to
-1.0) at relatively low cost, so this shouldn't have any negative impact
on the benchmarks.

Note the p values (no significant difference):

Summary of cpu time and (wall-clock time):
                    best    avg      sd     +/-   p   (best)    (avg)      (sd)     +/-   p
     pathological 1.07000 1.16800 0.12734 [+0.9%]   (1.07308) (1.17285) (0.13029) [+0.6%]
        command-t 0.81000 0.92000 0.09592 [+2.4%]   (0.81280) (0.92122) (0.09806) [+2.6%]
chromium (subset) 3.18000 3.30600 0.09521 [-3.0%]   (0.64119) (0.67648) (0.02236) [-2.5%]
 chromium (whole) 4.30000 4.34200 0.03370 [-1.2%]   (0.63329) (0.67998) (0.02648) [-8.9%]
       big (400k) 6.23000 6.39400 0.12532 [-0.7%]   (0.99223) (1.06572) (0.07311) [+3.2%]
c

diff --git a/ruby/command-t/ext/command-t/match.c b/ruby/command-t/ext/command-t/match.c
index 7a28458..bc3ee40 100644
--- a/ruby/command-t/ext/command-t/match.c
+++ b/ruby/command-t/ext/command-t/match.c
@@ -151,7 +151,7 @@ float calculate_match(
             for (i = 0; i < m.haystack_len; i++) {
                 char c = m.haystack_p[i];
                 if (c == '.' && (i == 0 || m.haystack_p[i - 1] == '/')) {
-                    return 0.0;
+                    return -1.0;
                 }
             }
         }
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `ruby/command-t/ext/command-t/match.c`**
   - **Line Change**: The return value for the condition checking if a character is a dot ('.') has been modified. 
   - **Before**: The function returned `0.0` when a dot was encountered, which effectively hid dotfiles from the search results.
   - **After**: The function now returns `-1.0` when a dot is encountered, which allows dotfiles to be considered in subsequent searches.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `match.c` addresses a regression issue introduced in a previous commit (ee9732511). By changing the return value from `0.0` to `-1.0`, the patch ensures that dotfiles are not immediately hidden from search results when the search string is initially empty. Instead, they are marked with a negative score, which allows them to be included in the search results if the user types a period ('.') subsequently. This change maintains the intended functionality of the search feature while preventing dotfiles from being skipped inappropriately, thus improving user experience without significantly impacting performance.
